content.comment_body: Hello everyone, this is my first post here as I’m new to [product_name]. My goal is to connect the PLC to a residential router and enable control from an iPhone. Ultimately, I’d like to use it as a swimming pool controller, but for now, I’m running a test program to learn how to use the [product_name] Web Editor for device control via iPhone, Android, or PC. I can access the PLC through a browser when it’s connected directly to my laptop, but when plugged into the router, I’m unable to reach it from the laptop. This is an initial step before using [product_name] Web Editor—I expected to access the PLC through the router as easily as direct connection. Any advice would be appreciated. Thanks.

Generally speaking, if the direct PLC-to-PC connection works but it fails through the router, the issue may be related to router settings (like missing port forwarding). Since you want to control the PLC from an iPhone, you might also be looking for remote access beyond your local network. More precise details on your setup would help.
I’m not sure what you mean regarding port releases on my router. Yes, my goal is to enable access to the PLC from a phone or PC, even when I’m not at home.
Are you able to connect to the PLC with your iPhone when on the home network?

Thank you for your support—I’m new to this. I believe I need [product_name] Web Editor to connect, and I haven’t downloaded any app. My first step was plugging the PLC into the router so I can try accessing it from the PC on my network. Then, my plan is to use [product_name] Web Editor next.
Once the PLC is connected to the router, can you access its web server from the PC within your home network? Have you enabled access under the web server’s access control settings?

I’m unclear about accessing the web server. When I enter the IP address in my browser with the PLC plugged into the router, it times out and won’t connect. But when the PLC is directly linked to the PC, entering the IP address works—I can log in, interact with variables, and see inputs/outputs. I’ve already set up access permissions and passwords.
Go to “Tools > Transfer > Access Control” and establish the connection. Set the appropriate check marks and passwords, then click the 'Apply' button in those fields.

Thanks for your help—I rechecked the setup. While connected to the router, I had to change the interface to the wireless adapter. Your suggestion that the connection should have worked was spot on. I’ll likely have more questions and will aim to provide more specifics next time. Thanks again.
Glad it’s working now! Just a reminder: Without detailed information like mentioning WiFi use, it’s hard to provide precise help.

Hello again, I set up a sample project and used [product_name] Web Editor to create a custom page for my iPhone, but the device can’t connect to the PLC for login and site selection. Typing the IP (e.g., http://192.168.x.x) in Safari results in a timeout, and Chrome just keeps trying to connect. My laptop, however, can access the web server page created in [product_name] Web Editor and control the PLC without issue, both devices on the same router. I didn’t use HTTPS because root certificate setup instructions for iOS are unclear. I’m not sure how to get the screen described on page 320 of the [document], nor what steps to take if I did. I followed online tutorials and courses, but am still stuck on final steps for my test project. Any advice or requests for more details are welcome. Thanks in advance.

I’m still seeking help with this issue. I tried the suggested link, but didn’t find a solution there. The app won’t work either. I’m also attempting to set up cloud access, but haven’t succeeded, especially with AWS—the video guides don’t match my setup options in AWS. I’ve posted another forum thread for this, but haven’t received a response yet. Assistance would be appreciated.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experienced challenges connecting a [product_name] PLC to a home router for multi-device access. The main problem was the PLC being unreachable when routed through the home network, despite working via a direct PC connection. Solutions focused on network configurations, access controls, and interface settings. The key insight highlights users’ difficulty in initial network setup and the need for clearer, step-by-step guidance for web access across different devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward remote access and control of the PLC over their home network—and eventually remotely—using browsers on multiple devices, requiring minimal and easy-to-understand configuration.
